text:
oncall-bot: ALERT: multiple 5xx from elb-azb-prod, Route53 health-check failures detected for service 'inference-api' (region: euw1 standby, primary: azb). auto-escalation to on-call.

oncall-bot: Summary: Spikes in ELB latency and target health flapping in AZ-b (azb). A subset of targets in the azb ASG are becoming unhealthy, Route53 weighted record seeing increased latency -> slow DNS failover observed. Paging SRE.

pagerduty: Paging -> sre-alex (primary oncall) for INC-1902468023 (networking / elb route53)

sre-alex: saw alerts, joining. tl;dr: 502/504s for inference-api across several frontend pods, ELB 5xx counters jumping. Checking ELB target group health and ASG events now.

netops-jamie: I can see abnormal TCP retransmits to instances in azb from the ELB. Also saw increased SYN_RECV on a few instances. Could be network hypervisor flapping in AZ.

eng-maya: Canary traces show requests for long-lived streams timing out after ~10s then 502 returned. Backend (model-serving) logs show no OOMs, but connection resets from kernel.

sre-alex: running quick health checks + listing ELB target status

```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:123456:targetgroup/tg-inference/abcd
```

sre-alex: ~40% targets in azb marked Unhealthy/initial. Other AZs fine. Route53 healthchecks triggered; our weighted policy supposed to failover to euw1, but TTL is 60s and clients still hitting azb ELB -> lots of client errors.

support-lena: seeing customer tickets from two large tenants reporting increased 502s and streaming disconnects. Notified sales and tier-2.

pm-katie: can we send an external incident note? Need to quantify customer impact first.

netops-jamie: immediate mitigation options: 1) force deregister unhealthy targets in azb to drain them (fast-path), 2) scale up healthy AZs and re-register, 3) update Route53 weights to shift traffic off azb quicker.

sre-alex: plan: 1) reduce ELB target weight in azb (if weighted routing internal), 2) decrease route53 health-check failure threshold / lower TTL temporarily to speed failover, 3) start a controlled drain of suspect instances. Will coordinate with eng-maya for graceful shutdown.

eng-maya: for drains, use SIGTERM to pods to let model runtime finish current in-flight tokens. For host-level we can set deregistration delay to 10s.

sre-alex: executing step 1 - patch Route53 record weight -> switching 0->primary to euw1 70% (manual to accelerate)

```
# example (ops runbook)
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"inference.example.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"azb","Weight":10,"AliasTarget":{"HostedZoneId":"ZELB","DNSName":"elb-azb.amazonaws.com.","EvaluateTargetHealth":true}}]}}'
```

netops-jamie: also lowered Route53 health check failure threshold from 3->2 to speed detection. TTL reduced from 60 -> 15s.

support-lena: posting a brief Customer Notice draft to #general and to status page: "We are experiencing elevated errors and latency affecting inference-api in EU AZ-b. Engineers are investigating and routing traffic to alternate AZs/region. Updates every 15m." Want to post?

pm-katie: go ahead, keep it conservative.

sre-alex: initiating drain on 6 suspect instances in azb (deregistration delay 10s). Command:

```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn <tg-arn> --targets Id=i-0abc1,i-0abc2,i-0abc3
aws autoscaling set-instance-health --instance-id i-0abc1 --health-status Unhealthy
```

eng-maya: models on those hosts reported graceful shutdowns; streaming sessions dropped but retried to euw1.

netops-jamie: after drains, ELB 5xx rate dropped ~65% in 3m. Route53 failover triggered more clients to euw1. Latency trending down.

support-lena: customer ticket storm slowed. Two customers still seeing intermittent 5xx — likely cached DNS or long-lived connections.

pm-katie: update status page with mitigation note and ETA for full recovery 30-45m.

sre-alex: starting to scale up capacity in healthy AZs (increase ASG desired count + spin standby instances in euw1); also monitoring degraded EBS throughput in azb — some IO errors observed earlier; may be correlated.

netops-jamie: filing an AWS case: suspected AZ network fabric issue causing packet drops to a subset of instances. Case opened with support, ref AWS-INC-190246.

pagerduty: handoff reminder - screencap with summary then pass to next oncall in 30m (sre-alex -> eng-maya for stabilization)

eng-maya: taking lead for stabilization and customer comms. will stay on until metrics normalized and tickets cleared.

sre-alex: handing over: summary + runbook steps executed + current state: 2xx success rate back to 95%, 5xx count down to baseline, Route53 weights at euw1:80 azb:20, TTL 15s. Continuing watch.

support-lena: posted update to status page and customer emails sent to impacted accounts.

pm-katie: follow-up tasks: postmortem, quantify request loss, evaluate lowering default Route53 TTLs + faster health check thresholds for critical services. Also consider automatic cross-AZ weight rebalancer.

eng-maya: agreed. I'll log actions in INC-1902468023 and start a root cause investigation. Please attach any ASG/ELB instance ids and EBS error logs to the ticket.

netops-jamie: adding AWS case ID and packet captures to the incident ticket.

sre-alex: great work team. keep the watch for another 30m then close if stable.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-1902468023 updated: status -> mitigated. Next update in 30m for closure.

support-lena: closing loop on customer tickets, asked customers to confirm service recovery. :thumbsup:

eng-maya: will draft action items for postmortem. thanks all.
